pageCache.text:
The children here are genuinely cared for, nurtured and supported to grow and become the best they can be.
Pupils say that teachers make learning fun.
Pupils' well-being is given top priority.
Pupils have a strong sense of courageous advocacy with an ability to speak out confidently for justice for others locally, nationally and globally.
Teachers have ignited a love for learning
It doesn't matter which teacher you have, because all of them are really good with us and take care of us.
Shepherdswell Church of England Primary School
Welcome to Shepherdswell Church of England Primary School.
I feel incredibly proud to be the Headteacher of such a wonderful school community.
We are one of the most consistently successful schools, built on a foundation of outstanding teaching and learning. At the heart of everything we do is the belief that every child is unique. We set high expectations and provide the right balance of challenge and support so that every pupil can achieve their very best.
Our curriculum is exciting, creative and broad, making full use of our beautiful outdoor environment and Forest School. This allows our children to grow as happy, inquisitive and responsible learners who love discovering new things.
We are also delighted to have been awarded the Nurture UK Award in July 2025, recognising our commitment to supporting children’s wellbeing and personal development. Alongside this, we are proud to be developing as an established OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning) school, ensuring play is a rich, inclusive and joyful part of school life.
Our vision is to create an excellent school where everyone can flourish and grow. With God at the centre of our journey, our Christian values of Love, Gratitude, Justice and Determination guide all that we do and shape the caring, vibrant community we are so proud of.
I warmly invite you to explore our website and discover more about our school and we very much hope that you will want to become part of our story.
With best wishes,Mark Lamb Headteacher
If you would like a paper copy of anything on our website, then please contact the school office.

Breakfast and After School Club
Breakfast Club - daily from 7.45-8.30am The cost is £3.50
Children can attend the Breakfast Club on a regular basis or as an occasional user. Please book places in advance. All bookings for Breakfast Club should be via the School Comms App. If your child attends without a prior booking, a £2.00 additional charge will be added. Please note that if your child has not been booked in and spaces are full, we may not be able to accomodate them on the day.
Please pay by using the School Comms APP
Breakfast Club is open for all children from EYFS to Year 6 and is run by teaching assistants. We aim to provide a safe, stimulating environment where parents can leave their children from 7:45am each morning. We serve a healthy breakfast of: toast, cereal, fruit juice and pancakes. After eating breakfast the children play low-level games, read books or do puzzles maintaining a fairly quiet calm atmosphere. At 8:30am go into class.
After School Club - daily from 3:15 to 5:45 (ASC phone number - 07840 570831)
There is a late collection charge of £3.00 for any child booked into the late session who is not collected by 5.45pm.
If you wish your child to attend the ASC you must complete an authorised copy of our admission form, which is available from the school office. The form must state the child’s usual address, telephone and emergency contacts. All bookings for After School Club should be via the School Comms App. If your child attends without a prior booking, a £2.00 additional charge will be added.
After School Club Admission Form
Please pay by using the School Comms APP
Under new curriculum guidelines, the ASC follows Early Years Foundation Stage for all children aged 4 and 5. This means that the children aged 4 and 5 are designated a key person who will be there to ensure your child’s well being, involvement and enjoyment is at the best it can be.
We aim for each child to look forward to coming to After School Club where he/she will experience adventure and excitement through play and friendship. Children’s preferences, not gender, are the deciding factor in what children do at the club. The ASC is managed by Teaching Assistants from the school, and this means that there are familiar faces for our younger children, and continuous care between school and after school care. During each session, the ASC team provide a healthy snack for the children (included in the cost of the session), catering for needs, wants, likes, dislikes! Sessions can be booked as a one off or on a regular basis, we can be flexible, to cater for your childcare needs.
Wrap Around Care Policy

PTA
Registered Charity Number 1207401
The Shepherdswell PTA is run by a committee who are all volunteers: we are parents, carers, friends, and community members – just like you! We come together with the focus of supporting the school to help enhance, enrich, and improve learning experiences for all the children. We plan and run several events throughout the school year to raise money for our school and to give the children memorable experiences. We organise bake sales, school discos, break the rules days, and other special events for the children to enjoy.
But that’s not all we do. We also exist to bring school life and home life closer together - because it makes sense for parents to be involved in their child’s life at school. Some of these events include a Christmas fair, a summer fête, and family games nights to name just a few.
But to do all this we need help. Maybe you can come to a meeting and share your ideas, help set up an event, or run a stall. Perhaps you have a skill which could help us run more efficiently. Even if you are tight on time, many of our volunteering tasks can be done from home. We need people to design posters, wrap presents, organise tombola prizes, and put hampers together. The more people that become involved, the more we can achieve and the easier it will be.
If you’re interested in getting involved or have any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch. You can contact us at pta@shepherdswell.kent.sch.uk or just stop any of the committee members on the playground for a quick chat. We’re always happy to help and look forward to meeting all the newest members of the Shepherdswell School community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School Fridays - Shepherdswell Primary School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Forest School - 2025/26
Outdoor Learning at Shepherdswell Primary School
We are very proud of our outdoor learning provision at Shepherdswell Primary School. Our dedicated Outdoor Learning Centre, together with our extensive school grounds, provides rich opportunities to enhance and support learning across the curriculum.
Outdoor learning actively promotes our school values and underpins our key learner characteristics: Wellbeing Warrior, Lifelong Learner, and Courageous Adventurer.
Our Outdoor Learning Centre
Our Outdoor Learning Centre is an inclusive space designed to support wellbeing, curiosity, and hands-on learning. It is used by all children throughout the school day.
Sensory Garden
Our sensory garden was created and planted by the children. It includes a variety of herbs and plants that are explored through learning and used in cooking activities. The garden provides a calm, safe space where children can relax, reflect, and take responsibility for caring for their environment.
Learning Through Play and Exploration
We provide a wide range of large loose-parts resources that encourage:
These experiences help children grow as Wellbeing Warriors, develop as Lifelong Learners, and build confidence as Courageous Adventurers.
Teamwork
Communication
Physical and motor skill development
Creative and imaginative play
Problem-solving and resilience
Supporting OPAL Play
Our Outdoor Learning Centre also supports our OPAL approach to play. Children have access to the space not only during planned learning sessions, but also during dedicated playtimes.
Outdoor learning is a key part of life at Shepherdswell Primary School, helping children develop confidence, independence, wellbeing, and a strong connection with the natural world.

E-Safety
At Shepherdswell the children regularly use the internet as part of their learning. In school we regularly remind the children how to stay safe online through ‘e-safety’ activities.
At home, children are not always supervised when they are using the internet. This can potentially allow children access to a whole world of information and online communities, some of which may be unsuitable for children to access.
Whilst the internet is a wonderful place, we need to make sure that our children are safe and responsible internet users.
Here are some useful tips and links to keep your children safe online:

Illness, Health & NHS
As per the Government's website:
It can be tricky deciding whether or not to keep your child off school, nursery or playgroup when they're unwell.
There are government guidelines for schools and nurseries about health protection and managing specific infectious diseases at GOV.UK. These say when children should be kept off school and when they shouldn't.
If you do keep your child at home, it's important to phone the school or nursery on the first day. Let them know that your child won't be in and give them the reason.
If your child is well enough to go to school but has an infection that could be passed on, such as a cold sore or head lice, let their teacher know.
